prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, and its first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators first. This is a new state of matter in the sense the committee has traditionally valued. Kane and Mele supplied a symmetry-based classification with a clean invariant, and the Molenkamp group then measured the predicted edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells. The idea has been confirmed across many material families (HgTe, InAs/GaSb, Bi-based compounds, ARPES on 3D topological insulators) and the interpretation has been stable for close to twenty years, so the recognition is neither premature nor contested on the physics. Band-structure theory, DFT-based materials work and spectroscopy have all been used to identify and refine the materials, which is the quantitative link between prediction and measurement that I trust most. The field has also grown into a general framework for topological matter, so the discovery has had large consequences.
statement.case_against: The main reservation is attribution. The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal of HgTe as the host material was decisive for the experiment, and Zhang's death means it cannot be repaired by adding him. The 3D topological insulator work (Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents, Roy, Hsieh-Hasan) is arguably as influential as the 2D case, and a three-person cap cannot cover it. The 2016 prize for topological phases also means the committee must be able to state clearly what is new here. If the committee cannot settle the credit or the framing, a cleaner configuration such as the lattice clocks would be the safer choice.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks the Aharonov-Bohm and Berry phase entry first as a unifying geometric concept, and he also notes that the Haldane-Thouless-Kosterlitz prize of 2016 reduces the marginal novelty of topological insulators.
responses.response: I take the 2016 overlap seriously, but I read it differently. The 2016 prize rewarded topological phase transitions and the quantum Hall-type topological invariants in specific model systems. Time-reversal-invariant Z2 phases are a distinct symmetry class, they need no magnetic field, and they were found in real materials by a decisive experiment. On B034, I agree that the Berry phase and Aharonov-Bohm effect are deep and underlie all of this, but I do not see one decisive experiment tied to the pair, and priority questions (Ehrenberg-Siday, Pancharatnam) and Bohm's death complicate the credit. I would value the concept more as a foundation than as the single prize-worthy discovery.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED first, but he ranks topological insulators sixth and flags both the 2016 overlap and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang gap in the credit.
responses.response: The BHZ gap is real and I raised it myself, so I do not dismiss it. It also appears in his own circuit QED entry, where Wallraff is missing, so neither candidate is cleanly attributed from the supplied names. For B048 the credited trio contains both the theory origin (Kane and Mele) and the first experiment (Molenkamp), whereas the Wallraff omission removes the lead experimentalist of the first strong-coupling demonstration. I also share his and Mehlig's concern that the 2025 prize on circuits makes another superconducting-circuit prize look close to a repeat. I would be glad to hear whether he sees the BHZ omission as disqualifying.

responses.point: Lindroth and Kroll rank the optical lattice clocks first, arguing that a quantitative, reproducible, mature result is the safest and most timely choice, and Lindroth also puts the Aharonov-Bohm and Berry phase entry fifth.
responses.response: I agree that the clocks are among the cleanest scientifically: independent laboratories agree at the 10^-18 level, and the attribution to Katori and Ye is far less contested than that of my own first choice. That is why I list B013 as my first alternative. My hesitation is only about kind: the clocks are a spectacular improvement in an established measurement capability, with the 2005 and 2012 prizes nearby, while the topological insulator is a new quantum state whose existence surprised theorists. I do not think broad first-place support alone should settle the question, but I would accept B013 if the committee judges the attribution of B048 too fragile.

responses.point: Olsson ranks aberration-corrected electron optics first as a genuine invention enabling sub-angstrom imaging, and she ranks the topological insulators third while flagging the BHZ omission and the fragility of the three-way credit.
responses.response: I agree with her on the fragility of the credit and I accept that the instrument entry has a very clean original-work split among Rose, Haider and Krivanek. As someone who relies on spectroscopy and microscopy to confirm theory, I value that work highly. My doubt is whether the committee will frame it as physics rather than instrumentation after the recent cryo-EM chemistry prize, and with only one first-place vote it has little support to build on. I would be open to reconsidering if she can show how it differs in kind from the instrument-led prizes we have already given.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks IceCube neutrino astronomy first and the magic-angle graphene entry fourth, stressing that nature supplied the clue and noting that the source identification is still accumulating.
responses.response: I defer to him on astroparticle physics, but his own note that the source associations are still developing is the same maturity concern I have about twisted bilayer graphene. For the moire entry I would also say the discovery is robust while the explanation of the superconductivity is not, so I place it below topological insulators, where the physical interpretation is settled. I would like to understand what the committee would want to see before IceCube source evidence counts as decisive.

uncertainties: Whether the missing Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang credit and the 3D topological insulator work make the three-name set unfair, and whether the prize should be framed around the 2D quantum spin Hall effect or the wider topological insulator concept.
Whether the committee regards time-reversal-invariant topological phases as sufficiently distinct from the 2016 prize.
Whether strong consensus support for the optical lattice clocks should outweigh my preference for a new-quantum-state discovery.
My recollection of the history is unverified, and I defer to colleagues on atomic clocks, astroparticle physics and circuit QED.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. My background in electronic-structure theory is close to the materials side of B048 and B041 and I use topological-material calculations, but I have no known personal, institutional or collaborative link to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp or the other credited names.
